description.narrative: The WATCH II Program aims at supporting i) the operationalization of the PRRH, and ii) the strategic role that Sweden will play as coleader of the Watershed Roundtable. The proposed activities have been organized around the three pillars of the National Watershed Plan, being also directly linked to Sweden’s current co-leadership of the Watershed Roundtable. The plan is based on using the watershed as a frame for planning and decision making to promote improved water resource management through citizen participation leading to enhanced climate resilience and better access to basic public services. The main objective of the Program is oriented to ensure that efforts to enhance the implementation of the new Watershed Plan increase the possibility that watershed planning will lead to on-the-ground changes that improve sustainable management of natural resources and living conditions for disadvantaged communities within a watershed.

WATCH II-programmet syftar till att stödja i) operationaliseringen av PRRH, och ii) den strategiska roll som Sverige kommer att spela som en part i det delade ledarskapet för det s.k Watershed Roundtable. De föreslagna aktiviteterna har organiserats kring de tre pelarna i den nationella vattenfördelningsplanen, som också direkt kopplat till Sveriges nuvarande del i ledarskapet av Watershed Roundtable. Den bygger på att använda vattenanvändning som en ram för planering och beslutsfattande för att främja förbättrad vattenresursförvaltning genom folkligt deltagande vilket leder till ökad klimatmotståndskraft och tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster och service. Programmets huvudmål är inriktat på att säkerställa att insatser för att förbättra genomförandet av den nya vattenfördelningsplanen ökar möjligheten för planering av vattenanvändning vilket leder till förändringar på plats som förbättrar en hållbar förvaltning av naturresurser och levnadsvillkoren för de grupper i samhället som är missgynnade vad avser tillgång till och användning av vatten.

The general objective of the contribution is to ensure that efforts to enhance the implementation of the new National Watershed Plan PPRH increase the possibility that watershed planning will lead to on-the-ground changes that improve sustainable management of natural resources and living conditions for disadvantaged communities within Bolivian watersheds.
The proposed activities have been organized around the three pillars of the PPRH, being also directly linked to Sweden current co-leadership of the Watershed RoundTable (four pillars) and five specific objectives. - Specific Objective 1: Support Sweden in its co-leadership function of the Watershed Coordination Roundtable and the Technical Assistane Rountable SubAT. -Specific Objective 2: Respond efficiently and in a timely manner to requests from the MMAyA for capacity building on the Bolivia WATCH Toolbox as an input to efforts to effectively and productively implement the PPRH. - Specific Objective 3: Design a Finance Unit within the MMAyA to identify promising intervention opportunities prioritized in prior PDCs and future Water Planning Strategy for a Watershed. (EPHICs in Spanish according to the new PPRH) and to move these interventions towards funding and implementation based on knowledge of and experience with the full range of potential sources of funding. - Specific Objective 4: Collaborate with international agencies participating in the Watershed Coordination Roundtable in ensure the delivery of at least two productive investments in watersheds where PDCs were developed during Bolivian Watch Phase 1 - Specific Objective 5: Continue to build the case, through a cross-cutting approach to program implementation, that explicit integration of sustainable sanitation approaches, as well as gender and poverty considerations. The main pillars are i) Pillar 0: Support to Swedish Embassy and VRHR, ii) Pillar 1. Efficient, effective, and participatory governance, with a focus on gender and social equity, iii) Pillar 2. Digital management with knowledge, science, and technology and iv) Pillar 3. Productive investments

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and Stiftelsen The Stockholm Environment Institute regarding Bolivia WATCH 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Main Results During the Reporting Period (2024 -2025) The principal achievements for the reporting period are organized according to the programs strategic pillars:
Pillar 0 Governance and Planning Instruments (cooperation platforms: GruS, MDC and SubAT) * Significant progress was achieved in the preparation of two policy briefsone on the harmonization of territorial and water sector planning, and another on sustainable sanitation and watershed management, achieving 70% of Indicator 1. * Ongoing support was provided to the Watershed Roundtable (MDC) and SubAT, including mapping of international cooperation efforts and proposing updates to its regulatory framework. For the preparation of the policy briefs, it was necessary to develop several supporting sub-products that provided the analysis and substantive inputs for the aforementioned documents, which are described below: * Evaluation of the 20212025 Plurinational Water Resources Plan (PPRH) using a Balanced Scorecard methodology. * Mapping and digitization of international cooperation efforts and tools for integration into national systems. * Drafting of regulatory updates and facilitation of collaborative meetings, providing documentary support for the forthcoming 20262030 Water Policy Planning Instrument.
Pillar 1 Governance and Strategic planning * Preparation of a policy brief with Bolivia WATCHs recommendations for the 20262030 Water Resources Policy, supported by analytical inputs from each center and local team, achieving 75% of Indicator 2. * The National Water Balance of Bolivia (BHNB) has been successfully scaled up and integrated into sectoral planning instruments across the Ministry of Environment and Water (MMAyA), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MRE), and the Ministry of Development Planning (MPD). Additionally, the Basin Master Plans (PDC) of Tupiza, Pampa Huari, and Cotagaita have been expanded to guide pre-investment and public investment instruments in the corresponding municipalities. Against a target of six instruments, a total of thirteen have been achieved, achieving 217% of Indicator 3. * One of two planned water quality monitoring campaigns was completed in the Tupiza and Pampa Huari rivers, enabling MMAyA to fund four complementary studies on river classification and recovery. Support was also provided to GAD Potosí to strengthen the SIMOVH system, achieving 67% of Indicator 4. * Technical contribution was made in drafting two concept notes for Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) projects in transboundary basins (Madera-Madeira and Madre de Dios), aimed at securing climate finance through the Global Environment Facility (GEF), achieving 100% of indicator 5. * Significant progress has been made in one of two educational basins, based on the project work to recover mining land in the Cayara Basin (Pampa Huari), with the participation of the platform (social council), achieving 50% of indicator 6.
Pillar 2 Strengthening capacities and institutions * One master's thesis, "WASH and Food Security: An analysis of water governance in Bolivia," was guided and framed within SEI-BW2's work to contribute to the sanitation sector (Katherine Rivas - Jönköping University), achieving 50% of indicator 7. * Transition to a scalable online training model (MOOC-Massive Online Open Course). In partnership with ELME and the Universidad Autónoma Tomás Frías (UATF), an online WEAP Level 1 course was developed and delivered, with 87 registered participants, of whom 63 successfully completed the course, achieving 83% of Indicator 8. * Adoption of digital learning methods enabled the program to absorb a budget reduction of 300,000 SEK without compromising deliverables. Pillar 3 Applied Research and Innovation (Investments with a territorial focus) * BW2 seed capital was used to promote two pilot projects implementing actions by the Alta La Paz PDC (Chinchaya WWTP in family farming in partnership with Aguatuya and EPSAS for wastewater reuse) and the Pampa Huari PDC (Villacollo reforestation project). Third-party funds were also leveraged for the following projects (Indicator 10): - IICA BO-AD-015 (EuroClima-AECID): Ecological flow modeling in the Lípez region of Potosí using WEAP. - World Bank: Development of protocols and processes for accessing data from the Bolivia Surface Water Balance WEAP. - BID BO-T1419-P004: Watershed Planning Strategy for the Acre River Basin (EPHIC ACRE).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
